real_s1.explanation: This unit responds to small fluffy or long-haired dogs (toy breeds, terriers, spaniels) and similar furry animals. Within those classes it is most active when the subject faces or points to the image's right, and least active when it faces left. It also prefers subjects centered horizontally rather than placed in the right third. Similar units share a general preference for large, frontal subjects, but the right-facing preference is particular to this unit.

real_s2.explanation: This unit responds to small, fluffy, long-haired dogs (toy terriers, spaniels, Maltese and similar breeds) when the animal is facing or pointing to the right, or toward or away from the camera, rather than to the left. Its clearest distinguishing trait is the direction preference, especially right over left, where the similar units are not unusual. It also prefers subjects centered horizontally over ones in the right third.

real_s3.explanation: The unit responds to small, fluffy, long-haired toy dogs and similar furry faces, and it fires more when the animal faces right rather than left. A right-facing subject is distinctive for this unit compared with its similar units, which respond to frontal or close framing instead. The unit also prefers a centered subject that fills the frame, but the similar units share that preference.

null_s1.explanation: The unit responds most to small, long-haired toy and terrier breeds (Maltese, Shih-Tzu, Dandie Dinmont, Westie, Pekinese, Lhasa), with fluffy fur as the common feature. Within those classes it is more active when the dog fills a moderate part of the frame rather than nearly all of it. It is also more active under medium rather than bright lighting and in photos with a warm color tint. Medium lighting is partly shared with one similar unit, but the framing and warm-tint preferences are more specific to this unit.

null_s2.explanation: The unit responds most to small, long-haired toy and terrier dogs (Maltese, Shih-Tzu, Dandie Dinmont, Westie, Pekinese) and related furry animals. It is also more active when the subject is under medium rather than bright light, and when the photo has a warm tint. null_s3.explanation: The unit is most active on small fluffy, long-haired toy and terrier breeds (Maltese, Shih-Tzu, Lhasa, Yorkshire terrier and similar). Within those classes it prefers a medium-framed subject, one taking up a quarter to three quarters of the photo, over a tight close-up. It also prefers moderate rather than bright lighting and a warm color tint, so it seems tuned to the dog's furry body seen at a moderate scale under warm, indoor-style light.
